effect_mechanism: Wetlands buffer communities from coastal storm surges, reduce wave damage and floods, and stabilise shorelines; the Ramsar briefing note presents this as a reason why wetland protection and restoration increase climate resilience as storms, flooding, droughts and heat waves become more frequent [ev_wet_flood_hazard_ramsar18_2].
conditionality: This row rests on a single institutional review, a Ramsar Convention briefing note on wetland restoration and climate resilience, and the flood statement is one of its key messages rather than a measured result [ev_wet_flood_hazard_ramsar18_2]. effect_mechanism: Wetlands cool the local climate by spending incoming energy on evaporation: in measurements at Trebon, Czech Republic, up to 60% to 70% of solar energy was transformed into sensible heat over a drained crop field against only 5% to 10% over an intact wetland, where 70% to 80% of heat is dissipated via evapotranspiration [ev_wet_microclimate_buffering_ramsar18_1].
conditionality: This row rests on a single institutional review, a Ramsar Convention briefing note on wetland restoration and climate resilience, which reproduces measurements from one temperate, high-income site [ev_wet_microclimate_buffering_ramsar18_1]. The comparison is between an intact wetland and a drained field, so it shows the target state of restoration rather than a measured gain at a restored site, and local cooling is a component of heat stress rather than a measure of heat stress on people, crops or livestock.
